turns.text:
9:45 pm update. day 2 solo, the baby is winning 14-0 🙃

theo will only nap if he's held. he sleeps in the crib in the nursery half of the spare room with the white noise on rain, and at night that's fine, but all morning he went off like a smoke alarm the second i put him down. i paced the apartment for what felt like a full marathon. got one 25 min crib nap total.

need tips for getting him to nap in the crib without being held. please and thanks. in table form if you can, i think better in tables

Day 2 solo is a rough scoreboard, but contact-only naps are very common at this age and very fixable. Here's a plan in table form:

| Lever | What to try | Why it helps |
|---|---|---|
| Wake window | Aim to start the nap routine before he's overtired. Watch for early cues (staring off, eye rubbing, jerky movements), not just the clock | Overtired babies fight the crib hardest |
| Mini routine | 5 minutes, same every time: dim the room, swaddle or sleep sack, a song, the same phrase, then down | Gives him a predictable signal that sleep is next |
| Drowsy but awake | Put him down calm and sleepy, not fully out | Teaches him to do the last step himself |
| Room setup | Dark room (blackout curtains), white noise at a steady volume, comfortable temperature. Keeping the rain sound you already use is good | Daytime light is a big nap-wrecker |
| Hands-on, not held | Once he's down, keep a hand on his chest, shush or pat rhythmically, then slowly lift your hand | A bridge between being held and being alone |
| The pause | If he fusses, wait 1-2 minutes before picking him up, and soothe in the crib first | Gives him a chance to settle |
| Gradual shift | Day 1: hold until drowsy, then down. Day 2: rock less. Day 3: hand-on only | Changes things in small steps |
| Expectations | Short crib naps (25-40 min) are normal while he learns. Consistency matters more than any one nap | One bad morning doesn't undo anything |

If you have a feeling for how long he's awake between naps, tell me and I can suggest a window to try. And if the crying escalates or you're ever worried about him, his pediatrician is the right person to call.

thanks, this is great. his wake windows are about 90 min. and nights are tight for me, i just did the baby laundry tonight in the card-only laundry room downstairs so i'm running on fumes. i also packed my wife's lunch last night so her mornings stay easy, so i don't have a ton of evening bandwidth for a big overhaul. what's the lowest effort version of this?

That's a lot to carry, so here's the low-effort version. Pick just three things:

| Step | Effort | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Watch the clock | Almost none | Start winding down at about 75-80 minutes awake, before the 90-minute mark, so he isn't already overtired |
| 2. Same 3-minute routine | Low | Dim the room, sleep sack, same song or phrase, rain noise on, then down while drowsy |
| 3. Hand on, then out | Low | Keep a hand on his chest and pat or shush. Wait a minute or two before picking him up if he fusses |

Skip everything else for now. Don't worry about blackout curtains, a new schedule or a full training plan this week.

Tonight, you could do one thing for tomorrow's first nap: decide the exact routine and the song so you're not improvising while he's wound up.

Expect short crib naps for a few days. That's normal progress. If tomorrow goes badly, it's one data point, not a verdict. Want me to write a tiny cue card you can tape up in the nursery?
yes please, short version. cue card

**Nap Cue Card**

1. Awake ~75-80 min? Start now.
2. Dim room, rain noise on, sleep sack.
3. Same song, same phrase.
4. Down drowsy, not asleep.
5. Hand on chest, pat or shush.
6. Fuss? Wait 1-2 min, soothe in the crib first.
7. Short nap = still a win.

Good luck tomorrow. Dad 1, nap 1 is within reach. 🙂
